text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Food concern CSM takes over U.S. producer/distributor of bakery ingredients, Karp's. (p1)
- J&J Investments, major shareholder in car dealership Air Holding, considers bidding for remaining shares. (p1)
- Food producer Nutricia and Friesland Dairy Foods in talks on merging and transferring some activities. (p1)
- Eurolist, aimed at creating a premier league of European companies, on the verge of collapse. (p1)
- Dutch PTT (KPN) losing millions of guilders on 16.3 pct stake in joint venture UMC in the Ukraine. (p3)
- Chemicals concern DSM will not fully aim at offering shareholders value, but will hold on to business value. (p3)
- ABN Amro bank eyes France's bank Banque Demachy Worms. (p3)
- Wholesaler group Sligro takes over three firms, adding Dfl 25 million to turnover. (p4)
VOLKSKRANT
- Cut-rate airline EasyJet wins fight against KLM's ad campaign for cheap flights to London, Paris and Berlin. (p2)
- Finance minister Gerrit Zalm favours safety net for life-insurers in financial trouble. (p2)
- PTT Telecom's GSM mobile phone network grows faster than that of rival Libertel. (p2)
- Agricultural futures market ATA stops trading in wheat contracts, which were introduced last year. (p17)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Bank insurer ING gets licence from Canadian government. (p29)
- OECD forecasts three percent economic growth for the Netherlands in 1997. (p29)
- Philips Electronics sells data-communication activities to French telecoms group Compagnie des Signaux. (p31)
- Chemicals concern Hoechst Holland sells unit Trespa Int. to HAL investments. (p33)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Within 10 years, telecommunications via satellite will be as normal as it is with a GSM phone now, according to KPN unit station 12. (p13)
- Printer maker Oce van der Grinten buys remaining 70 pct of shares in Canada's Abso Blue Prints. (p15)
TROUW
- Dutch railway operator NS and European partners, Hermes Europe Rail, to build phone network in Britain. (p7)
